A_target.statement:
Let $p$ be a [[Definition:Prime Number|prime]].
The [[Definition:P-adic Norm|$p$-adic absolute value]] on $\Q$ satisfies:
:$\size {x y}_p = \size x_p \size y_p$
:$\size {x + y}_p \le \max \set {\size x_p, \size y_p}$
and the [[Definition:Completion of Metric Space|completion]] $\Q_p$ of $\Q$ under it is a [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete]] [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Absolute Value|absolute value]] on $\Q$ satisfies $\size {x y} = \size x \size y$ and $\size {x + y} \le \size x + \size y$, and the completion of $\Q$ under it is $\R$.

substitutions.Cauchy sequences for the usual metric: Cauchy sequences for the p-adic metric

derived.the completion is a field: the p-adic numbers form a field, by the same construction
derived.the triangle inequality: the ultrametric inequality, which is strictly stronger

object_map.reformulation: Swap the absolute value for a different one satisfying the same axioms, then rerun the completion construction unchanged.

validity_conditions: The completion construction uses only the axioms of an absolute value, so it applies verbatim once multiplicativity and the triangle inequality are checked.
The p-adic inequality is ultrametric, which is stronger than the triangle inequality, so every consequence of the latter still holds and additional facts become available.
Order-dependent and Archimedean facts do not transfer: the p-adic numbers carry no compatible order and are totally disconnected, so the intermediate value theorem has no analogue.
proof_plan:
Form the [[Definition:Cauchy Sequence (Metric Space)|Cauchy sequences]] in $\Q$ modulo null sequences, exactly as in the construction of $\R$.
The result $\Q_p$ is a complete field.
